card.name: Singular/plural markers in dosing text
card.fires_on: Marks where a noun's number is unclear or optional, such as the "(s" in "dose(s)" and "toxin(s)", or the end of a product name like TDS after "only one". It also fires weakly on words like "potential" and "is" after "a" or "any of these".

modes.label: Optional plural "(s)"
modes.description: The opening of a parenthetical (s) added to a noun to mean one or more.
modes.example: Studies indicate a toxin<<(s>>) produced by Clostridia is one

modes.label: Single patch wording
modes.description: The last piece of a patch name such as TDS after "only one".
modes.example: Instruct women to wear only one TWIRLA T<<DS>> at any time.

modes.label: Number-agreement words
modes.description: A verb or word like "potential" or "is" right after a singular noun phrase.
modes.example: There is a<< potential>> for venous and arterial thrombotic

card.writes: It nudges the next words toward ones that list or refer back to several items, like "themselves", "examples" and Chinese "respectively".
card.plain: It fires where the text is deciding whether a thing is one or several, like "dose(s)" or "only one patch".
